rulings.restated: Input — Is all your investment in this business at risk (box 32a)? Answer no if any of these is invested in it: a nonrecourse loan used to finance the business, buy property used in it, or buy the business, that is not secured by your own property other than property used in the business and that you are not personally responsible to repay; cash, property or borrowed money protected against loss by a guarantee, stop-loss agreement or similar arrangement (casualty and tort-liability insurance do not count); money borrowed for use in the business from someone who has an interest in it other than as a creditor, or from a person related (under section 465(b)(3)(C)) to someone other than you who has such an interest
rulings.model: IRS instructions state 'there is an exception for certain nonrecourse financing borrowed by you in connection with holding real property'; the restatement treats any such nonrecourse loan as not at risk and omits that exception.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; accepted over-refusal. A filer whose only nonrecourse financing is qualified real property financing answers no and is refused through sc.not_at_risk, though that financing is at risk; a refusal, never a wrong amount.
